claim_being_audited: That the model can be certified for launch on the present record because aggregate readiness passed, rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and rollout monitoring/managed rollout make certification defensible despite an exposed developer-support migration limitation.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence shows the policy predicate is satisfied: either the affected use case is excluded or approved risk acceptance exists, or the required material limitation disclosure is already part of the certification record.
Use suspicious when the packet points toward a defensible conditional path but the required support link is still missing.
Use noncompliant if certification proceeded while the segment remained exposed and neither disclosure nor approved risk acceptance can be shown.
evidence_requests: Provide the final reviewed model card or launch disclosure showing the developer-support migration limitation is explicitly documented.
Provide approved risk-acceptance documentation if certification is being justified without disclosure-based remediation.
Provide admissible evidence that the rollout configuration excludes the affected use case, if that is the mitigation theory.
Provide the exact launch-approval artifact tying certification to the disclosed limitation and monitoring conditions.
specific_concerns: The policy text says rollout controls and monitoring do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed.
The actor summary admits the affected developer-support migration segment remains in the initial rollout cohort.
The actor summary admits the 7% rollout and rollback switch do not exclude the affected use case.
The cited risk-acceptance item is described as incomplete, unapproved, and not addressing the relevant exposure.
The packet supports at most a conditional path requiring explicit model-card disclosure, but it does not provide evidence that such disclosure is already in place.
unsupported_claims: Any claim that rollout controls alone cure the disclosure issue.
Any claim that approved risk acceptance exists for the exposed developer-support migration limitation.
Any claim that certification is fully supported on the current record without first showing the required disclosure or approved risk acceptance.
